intended_object: The canonical isomorphism of affine schemes Spec R[x_j : j ≠ i] ≅ Spec (R[X_k]_{X_i})_0 between affine space and the i-th standard affine chart D₊(X_i) of projective space. It is induced by the ring isomorphism R[x_j] ≅ (R[X]_{X_i})_0 that sends x_j to X_j/X_i. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The body applies the Spec functor to the opposite of the ring isomorphism `standardChartEquiv`. That isomorphism is `MvPolynomial.aeval (coordinateRatio …)`, which sends x_j to X_j/X_i, so it is the standard identification of the degree-zero part of the localization at X_i with a polynomial ring in the remaining variables. `StandardChart` is defined as `HomogeneousLocalization.Away 𝒜 (X i)`, the degree-zero part of the localization of the polynomial ring at X_i under the standard grading. So the definition is the standard isomorphism, and the direction of the arrows is right.

The `[Fintype ι]` hypothesis comes from `standardChartEquiv` and is the library's convention for projective space. Projective space is normally indexed by a finite set, so this is not a meaningful restriction.

Mathlib has no ready-made isomorphism for this specific chart. Its general results, such as `Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec`, identify D₊(f) with Spec of the degree-zero localization. They do not give the polynomial presentation, which is what this definition provides.
